solve.work: A section of a cone parallel to its base is a circle (smaller than the base).

questions.skill: Measure a circular cross-section
questions.stem: A sphere has a diameter of 18 centimeters. A plane passes through its center. What is the radius, in centimeters, of the circular cross-section?
questions.solution: A plane through the center cuts the sphere in its largest circle, which has the same radius as the sphere. The radius is $18 \div 2 = 9$ centimeters.

solve.work: A plane through the centre gives a great circle, with the sphere's radius: 18/2 = 9.

questions.skill: Name the solid formed by rotating a triangle
questions.stem: A right triangle is rotated $360^\circ$ about its hypotenuse. Which solid does it form?
choices: One cone with a cylinder inside it
A cylinder with a cone on top
Two cylinders joined end to end
Two cones joined at their bases
questions.answer: Two cones joined at their bases
questions.solution: The hypotenuse is the axis. The two legs sweep out two cones that have the same circular base, where the right-angle corner travels, so the solid is two cones joined at their bases.

solve.answer: Two cones joined at their bases
solve.work: The hypotenuse is the axis. The right-angle vertex traces a circle of radius equal to the altitude to the hypotenuse; each leg sweeps a cone with that circle as base. Two cones joined at their common base.

questions.skill: Measure a cross-section of a prism, pyramid or cylinder
questions.stem: A rectangular prism measures 4 centimeters by 5 centimeters by 9 centimeters. A plane cuts it parallel to the 4-by-5 face. What is the perimeter, in centimeters, of the cross-section?
questions.solution: A cut parallel to the 4-by-5 face is a 4-by-5 rectangle. Its perimeter is $2(4 + 5) = 18$ centimeters.

solve.work: Cut parallel to the 4-by-5 face gives a 4 by 5 rectangle; perimeter 2(4+5) = 18.

questions.skill: Name the cross-section of a solid
questions.stem: A plane cuts a square pyramid parallel to its base, between the base and the tip. What is the cross-section?
choices: A square larger than the base
A square smaller than the base
questions.answer: A square smaller than the base
questions.solution: Slices parallel to the base of a pyramid are similar to the base. The base is a square and the slice is closer to the tip, so it is a smaller square.

solve.answer: A square smaller than the base
solve.work: A section parallel to the base is similar to the base, scaled by its distance from the apex over the height (<1): a square smaller than the base.

questions.skill: Measure a circular cross-section
questions.stem: A sphere has a radius of 13 centimeters. A plane cuts it at a distance of 5 centimeters from the center. What is the radius, in centimeters, of the circular cross-section?
questions.solution: The radius of the sphere, the distance 5 to the plane and the radius of the circle form a right triangle with hypotenuse 13. The circle radius is $\sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = \sqrt{144} = 12$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Possible and impossible cross-sections
questions.stem: Which of these shapes can never be a cross-section of a cube?
questions.solution: A plane meets a cube in straight segments along its flat faces, so the cross-section always has straight sides. A rectangle, a triangle (cutting off a corner) and a hexagon are all possible, but a circle has no straight sides.

solve.work: A cube's sections are polygons with 3 to 6 sides (triangle, square/rectangle, pentagon, hexagon); its faces are flat so no curved boundary: a circle is never possible.

questions.skill: Measure a cross-section of a prism, pyramid or cylinder
questions.stem: A cylinder has a radius of 5 centimeters and a height of 12 centimeters. A plane cuts it through the axis, perpendicular to the bases. What is the area, in square centimeters, of the cross-section?
questions.solution: The cross-section is a rectangle. Its width is the diameter, $2 \times 5 = 10$, and its height is 12. The area is $10 \times 12 = 120$ square centimeters.

solve.work: Section through the axis is a rectangle of width = diameter 10 and height 12: area 120.

questions.skill: Name the solid formed by rotating a flat shape
questions.stem: A semicircle is rotated $360^\circ$ about its straight edge (its diameter). Which solid does it form?
questions.solution: Each point of the curved edge sweeps out a full circle around the diameter, so together they make the whole surface of a sphere. It is a sphere, not a hemisphere, because the semicircle is rotated all the way around.

solve.work: Rotating a half-disc about its diameter sweeps the full sphere (the semicircle turns through 360, covering both halves).

questions.skill: Name the solid formed by rotating a triangle
questions.stem: An isosceles triangle is rotated $360^\circ$ about the line from its top vertex straight down to the middle of its base. Which solid does it form?
questions.solution: That line is the axis. The base of the triangle sweeps out a circle, and the two equal sides sweep out the slanted surface that meets at the top vertex, so the solid is a cone.

solve.work: The axis of symmetry splits it into two congruent right triangles; rotating about the altitude, it sweeps a cone with height = altitude and radius = half the base.

questions.skill: Measure a solid formed by rotation
questions.stem: A right triangle with legs of 6 centimeters and 8 centimeters is rotated $360^\circ$ about its 8-centimeter leg. What is the slant height, in centimeters, of the cone it forms?
questions.solution: The cone has radius 6 and height 8. Its slant height is the hypotenuse of the triangle, $\sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{100} = 10$ centimeters.

solve.work: Height 8, radius 6; slant height = hypotenuse = sqrt(36+64) = 10.

questions.skill: Name the cross-section of a solid
questions.stem: A plane cuts a triangular prism parallel to its two triangular bases. How does the cross-section compare with a base?
choices: It is a triangle congruent to a base
It is a triangle smaller than a base
questions.answer: It is a triangle congruent to a base
questions.solution: The sides of a prism run straight from one base to the other, so a slice parallel to the bases is an exact copy of the base: a congruent triangle.

solve.answer: It is a triangle congruent to a base
solve.work: A prism has a constant cross-section parallel to its bases: a triangle congruent to a base.

questions.skill: Name the cross-section of a solid
questions.stem: A plane is perpendicular to the line joining two opposite corners of a cube and passes through the center of the cube. What is the cross-section?
questions.solution: This plane meets six faces of the cube, in six segments of equal length, so the cross-section has six equal sides and equal angles: a regular hexagon.

solve.work: The plane through the centre perpendicular to a space diagonal cuts six edges at their midpoints, giving a regular hexagon of side s*sqrt2/2.

questions.skill: Measure a circular cross-section
questions.stem: A cone has a base radius of 10 centimeters and a height of 12 centimeters. A plane cuts it parallel to the base, 3 centimeters above the base. What is the radius, in centimeters, of the circular cross-section?
questions.solution: The plane is $12 - 3 = 9$ centimeters below the tip. The small cone cut off at the tip is similar to the whole cone, so its radius is $10 \times \frac{9}{12} = 7.5$ centimeters.

solve.work: 3 cm above the base is 9 cm below the apex. Radius scales: 10 * 9/12 = 7.5.

questions.skill: Name the solid formed by rotating a flat shape
questions.stem: A trapezoid has two right angles. Its parallel sides are 3 units and 7 units long, and the side between them, perpendicular to both, is 4 units long. It is rotated $360^\circ$ about that perpendicular side. What solid does it form?
choices: A cone with its tip cut off
Two cones joined at their bases
questions.answer: A cone with its tip cut off
questions.solution: The parallel sides sweep out two circles, with radii 3 and 7, in parallel planes 4 units apart. The slanted side joins them, so the solid is a cone with its tip cut off.

solve.answer: A cone with its tip cut off
solve.work: Rotating about the perpendicular side (height 4), the parallel sides become radii 3 and 7 of the two circular faces and the slanted side sweeps a cone surface: a frustum, i.e. a cone with its tip cut off.

questions.skill: Measure a solid formed by rotation
questions.stem: A right triangle has legs of 3 and 4 and a hypotenuse of 5. It is rotated $360^\circ$ about the hypotenuse. What is the radius of the circle traced by the right-angle corner?
questions.solution: The radius is the distance from the right-angle corner to the hypotenuse, which is the altitude to the hypotenuse. Using area, $\frac{1}{2}(3)(4) = \frac{1}{2}(5)h$, so $h = \frac{12}{5}$.

solve.work: The right-angle corner traces a circle whose radius is its distance to the hypotenuse, the altitude: 3*4/5 = 12/5 = 2.4.

questions.skill: Name the solid formed by rotating a flat shape
questions.stem: A rectangle is rotated $360^\circ$ about a line outside it that is parallel to two of its sides and does not touch it. Which solid does it form?
choices: Two cylinders joined end to end
questions.solution: The side nearest the line sweeps out the inside wall and the far side sweeps out the outside wall. The gap between the line and the rectangle leaves a hole, so the solid is a hollow cylinder.

solve.work: The rectangle never touches the axis, so the swept solid has a hole of radius equal to the gap: a hollow cylinder (tube).

questions.skill: Measure a solid formed by rotation
questions.stem: A rectangle 2 units wide and 9 units tall is placed to the right of a vertical line, with its left side 3 units from the line. It is rotated $360^\circ$ about that line to form a tube. What is the outer radius of the tube, in units?
questions.solution: The inner wall is 3 units from the axis. The far side of the rectangle is 2 units farther out, so the outer radius is $3 + 2 = 5$ units.

solve.work: Inner radius 3, the rectangle extends 2 further, so outer radius 3 + 2 = 5.

questions.skill: Name the solid formed by rotating a flat shape
questions.stem: A circle is rotated $360^\circ$ about a line in its own plane that does not touch the circle. Which solid does it form?
questions.solution: Each point of the circle travels around the line in a circle of its own, and the line does not touch the circle, so there is a hole in the middle. The solid is a doughnut shape, called a torus.

solve.work: A circle revolved about a coplanar line not meeting it sweeps a torus (doughnut).

questions.skill: Measure a cross-section of a prism, pyramid or cylinder
questions.stem: A square pyramid has a base with sides of 8 centimeters and a height of 6 centimeters. A plane cuts it parallel to the base, 3 centimeters above the base. What is the area, in square centimeters, of the cross-section?
questions.solution: The plane is halfway up, 3 centimeters from the tip. The slice is a square similar to the base with ratio $\frac{3}{6}$, so its side is $8 \times \frac{1}{2} = 4$ and its area is $4^2 = 16$ square centimeters.

solve.work: 3 cm above the base is halfway up (3 cm below the apex of a 6 cm pyramid); side scales by 3/6: 8*1/2 = 4; area 16.

questions.skill: Possible and impossible cross-sections
questions.stem: Which of these shapes can never be a cross-section of a cylinder?
questions.solution: A plane meets the curved wall of a cylinder in curves or in straight lines parallel to the axis, and the bases in straight segments. A circle (parallel to the bases), a rectangle (parallel to the axis) and an ellipse (a tilted cut) are possible, but no cut gives three straight sides.

solve.work: A cylinder's sections: circle (parallel to base), ellipse (tilted), rectangle (parallel to axis), or regions bounded by chords and elliptic arcs. A plane not parallel to the axis gives at most two straight edges; parallel to the axis gives a rectangle. A triangle is impossible.

questions.skill: Measure a solid formed by rotation
questions.stem: A square has diagonals of length 10. It is rotated $360^\circ$ about one of its diagonals. What is the radius of the widest circular cross-section of the solid?
questions.solution: The diagonals of a square are perpendicular and bisect each other. The two corners off the axis are each $10 \div 2 = 5$ from it, so the solid, two cones joined at their bases, has a widest circle of radius 5.

solve.work: Rotating a square about a diagonal gives two cones joined at bases; the widest circle is traced by the other two vertices, at distance half the other diagonal: 10/2 = 5.

questions.skill: Density from mass and volume
questions.stem: A metal block has a volume of 40 cubic centimeters and a mass of 316 grams. What is its density in grams per cubic centimeter?
questions.solution: Density = mass / volume = 316 / 40 = 7.9 grams per cubic centimeter.

questions.skill: Population density
questions.stem: A town has 12,000 people living on 8 square miles of land. What is its population density, in people per square mile?
questions.solution: Population density = people / area = 12000 / 8 = 1500 people per square mile.

questions.skill: Volume of a real object
questions.stem: A cylindrical can has a radius of 3 centimeters and a height of 10 centimeters. What is its volume in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: Volume = $\pi r^2 h$ = $\pi \cdot 3^2 \cdot 10 = 90\pi$ cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Volume of a real object
questions.stem: A rectangular fish tank is 60 centimeters long, 30 centimeters wide and 40 centimeters tall. How many liters does it hold when full? (1 liter is 1000 cubic centimeters.)
questions.solution: Volume = 60 x 30 x 40 = 72000 cubic centimeters. Dividing by 1000 gives 72 liters.

questions.skill: Density from mass and volume
questions.stem: A block of wood has a density of 0.6 grams per cubic centimeter and a volume of 500 cubic centimeters. What is its mass in grams?
questions.solution: Mass = density x volume = 0.6 x 500 = 300 grams.

questions.skill: Optimizing a design
questions.stem: A farmer has 40 meters of fence to enclose a rectangular pen. Which set of dimensions gives the greatest area?
questions.solution: Each pen has perimeter 40. The areas are 75, 96, 100 and 84 square meters, so the 10 by 10 pen is greatest.

solve.work: All options have perimeter 40. Areas: 96, 75, 100, 84. Greatest is 10 by 10.

questions.skill: Perimeter, surface area and cost
questions.stem: A cube-shaped gift box has edges of 5 inches. How many square inches of wrapping paper cover all of its faces, with no overlap?
questions.solution: A cube has 6 square faces, each 5 x 5 = 25 square inches, so 6 x 25 = 150 square inches.

questions.skill: Volume of a real object
questions.stem: A ball has a radius of 3 inches. What is its volume in cubic inches?
questions.solution: Volume of a sphere = $\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \frac{4}{3}\pi \cdot 27 = 36\pi$.

questions.skill: Volume as a function of one variable
questions.stem: A box is made from a 20-inch by 12-inch sheet of cardboard by cutting a square of side $x$ inches from each corner and folding up the sides. Which function gives the volume of the box?
questions.solution: The height is $x$. Cutting $x$ from both ends removes $2x$ from each side, so the base is $(20-2x)$ by $(12-2x)$. Volume = base x height.

solve.work: Base becomes (20-2x) by (12-2x), height x, so V = x(20-2x)(12-2x).

questions.skill: Density from mass and volume
questions.stem: A solid gold bar is 10 centimeters long, 5 centimeters wide and 2 centimeters tall. Gold has a density of 19.3 grams per cubic centimeter. What is the mass of the bar in grams?
questions.solution: Volume = 10 x 5 x 2 = 100 cubic centimeters. Mass = density x volume = 19.3 x 100 = 1930 grams.

questions.skill: Density from mass and volume
questions.stem: A cylindrical log has a radius of 10 centimeters, a length of 100 centimeters and a mass of 25120 grams. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. What is its density in grams per cubic centimeter?
questions.solution: Volume = 3.14 x 10 x 10 x 100 = 31400 cubic centimeters. Density = 25120 / 31400 = 0.8 grams per cubic centimeter.

questions.skill: Volume of a real object
questions.stem: A conical pile of sand has a diameter of 12 feet and a height of 5 feet. What is its volume in cubic feet?
questions.solution: The radius is 6 feet. Volume = $\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi \cdot 36 \cdot 5 = 60\pi$.

questions.skill: Optimizing a design
questions.stem: A rectangular pen is built against a barn wall, so only three sides need fence, and 60 meters of fence are used. If each of the two sides touching the wall is $x$ meters long, the area is $A(x) = x(60-2x)$ square meters. What is the greatest possible area?
questions.solution: A(x) = 60x - 2x^2 is a parabola opening down, with its vertex at x = 60 / 4 = 15. Then A(15) = 15 x 30 = 450 square meters.

questions.skill: Perimeter, surface area and cost
questions.stem: An open-top box (no lid) is 4 feet long, 3 feet wide and 2 feet tall. Its material costs 3 dollars per square foot. How many dollars does the material for the box cost?
questions.solution: Base: 4 x 3 = 12. Two long sides: 2 x (4 x 2) = 16. Two short sides: 2 x (3 x 2) = 12. Total 40 square feet, and 40 x 3 = 120 dollars.

solve.work: Base 4*3 = 12; two sides 4*2 = 8 each (16); two ends 3*2 = 6 each (12). Total 40 sq ft; cost 40*3 = 120.

questions.skill: Composite solids
questions.stem: A silo is a cylinder of radius 3 meters and height 10 meters with a hemisphere on top, with the same radius. What is its total volume in cubic meters?
questions.solution: Cylinder: $\pi \cdot 9 \cdot 10 = 90\pi$. Hemisphere: $\frac{2}{3}\pi \cdot 27 = 18\pi$. Total $108\pi$.

questions.skill: Population density
questions.stem: A county has a population density of 85 people per square mile and an area of 240 square miles. How many people live in the county?
questions.solution: Population = density x area = 85 x 240 = 20400.

questions.skill: Scaling a design
questions.stem: A cylindrical tank has its radius doubled while its height stays the same. By what factor is its volume multiplied?
questions.solution: Volume = $\pi r^2 h$. Doubling r multiplies $r^2$ by 4, so the volume is multiplied by 4.

solve.work: V = pi r^2 h; (2r)^2 = 4r^2, so volume is multiplied by 4.

questions.skill: Volume as a function of one variable
questions.stem: A box is made from a 20 cm by 14 cm sheet by cutting a 3 cm square from each corner and folding up the sides. What is the volume of the box in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: The base is (20 - 6) by (14 - 6), which is 14 by 8, and the height is 3. Volume = 14 x 8 x 3 = 336 cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Optimizing a design
questions.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 36 meters. Its width is $w$ meters, and its area is $A(w) = w(18 - w)$. Which width gives the greatest area?
questions.solution: A(w) = 18w - w^2 is a parabola opening down. Its vertex is at w = 18 / 2 = 9, a square of side 9 meters.

questions.skill: Density from mass and volume
questions.stem: A rectangular aquarium is 50 centimeters long, 30 centimeters wide and 40 centimeters tall. It is filled with water to three-fourths of its height. Water has a density of 1 gram per cubic centimeter. What is the mass of the water in kilograms?
questions.solution: The water is 30 cm deep, so its volume is 50 x 30 x 30 = 45000 cubic centimeters. At 1 gram per cubic centimeter that is 45000 grams, or 45 kilograms.

questions.skill: Density from mass and volume
questions.stem: A solid steel ball has a radius of 5 centimeters, and steel has a density of 8 grams per cubic centimeter. Use 3 for $\pi$. What is the mass of the ball in grams?
questions.solution: Volume = $\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$ = 4/3 x 3 x 125 = 500 cubic centimeters. Mass = 8 x 500 = 4000 grams.

questions.skill: Optimizing a design
questions.stem: A rectangular field is fenced with 120 meters of fence in total: the outer boundary plus one divider parallel to the two short sides, so the fence has 3 pieces of width $w$ and 2 pieces of length. The area is $A(w) = \frac{w(120-3w)}{2}$ square meters. What is the greatest possible area?
questions.solution: A(w) = 60w - 1.5 w^2 opens down, with its vertex at w = 60 / (2 x 1.5) = 20. Then A(20) = 20 x 60 / 2 = 600 square meters.

solve.work: A = (120w - 3w^2)/2, vertex at w = 120/6 = 20; A = 20*60/2 = 600. (Length 30, so w is the short side, consistent.)

questions.skill: Optimizing a design
questions.stem: An open-top box with a square base of side $x$ meters has a volume of 32 cubic meters. Its surface area is $S(x) = x^2 + \frac{128}{x}$ square meters. Which value of $x$ gives the smallest surface area?

questions.skill: Scaling a design
questions.stem: A scale model of a water tank has every length equal to one tenth of the real tank's. The model holds 2 liters. How many liters does the real tank hold?
questions.solution: Volume scales with the cube of the length factor. The real tank is 10 times as long in each direction, so its volume is 10^3 = 1000 times as great: 2 x 1000 = 2000 liters.

questions.skill: Volume as a function of one variable
questions.stem: A box is made from a 30 cm by 18 cm sheet by cutting a square of side $x$ from each corner, so $V(x) = x(30-2x)(18-2x)$ cubic centimeters. Which of these values of $x$ gives the greatest volume?

questions.skill: Composite solids
questions.stem: A grain silo is a cylinder of radius 6 meters and height 8 meters with a cone of height 3 meters on top. The cone has the same radius. What is the total volume in cubic meters?
questions.solution: Cylinder: $\pi \cdot 36 \cdot 8 = 288\pi$. Cone: $\frac{1}{3}\pi \cdot 36 \cdot 3 = 36\pi$. Total $324\pi$.

questions.skill: Population density
questions.stem: City A has 90,000 people on 30 square kilometers. City B has 64,000 people on 16 square kilometers. Which statement is true?
choices: City A is denser, with 3000 people per square kilometer against 4000
City B is denser, with 4000 people per square kilometer against 3000
City A is denser, because it has more people in total
City B is denser, with 400 people per square kilometer against 300
questions.answer: City B is denser, with 4000 people per square kilometer against 3000
questions.solution: City A: 90000 / 30 = 3000 per square kilometer. City B: 64000 / 16 = 4000 per square kilometer. City B is denser.

solve.answer: City B is denser, with 4000 people per square kilometer against 3000

questions.skill: Volume of a real object
questions.stem: A cylindrical can must hold 628 cubic centimeters and has a radius of 5 centimeters. Use 3.14 for $\pi$. How tall must the can be, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Volume = $\pi r^2 h$, so 628 = 3.14 x 25 x h = 78.5 h. Then h = 628 / 78.5 = 8 centimeters.

questions.skill: Optimizing a design
questions.stem: A rectangular lot must have an area of 400 square meters and be fenced all around. Which dimensions need the least fence?
questions.solution: Perimeters: 10 by 40 gives 100. 20 by 20 gives 80. 25 by 16 gives 82. 50 by 8 gives 116. The least fence is 80 meters, for 20 by 20.

solve.work: All have area 400. Perimeters: 100, 80, 116, 82. Least: 20 by 20.

questions.skill: Population and sample
questions.stem: A school has 900 students. The principal asks 60 randomly chosen students about the lunch menu. What is the population?
choices: The students who like the lunch menu
questions.solution: The population is the whole group we want to learn about: all 900 students. The 60 students asked are the sample.

solve.work: The population is the whole group of interest: all 900 students.

questions.skill: Population and sample
questions.stem: A factory makes 5,000 toys in a day. An inspector tests 50 toys chosen at random. Which group is the sample?
choices: All toys the factory has ever made
The toys that were not tested
questions.solution: The sample is the part of the population that is actually studied: the 50 toys that were tested.

solve.work: The sample is the subset actually tested: the 50 toys.

questions.skill: Random and biased sampling
questions.stem: Which is a random sample of the students in a school?
choices: The first 30 students who arrive at the cafeteria at lunch
Thirty students chosen from the honor roll
The 30 students who belong to the chess club
All names go in a bin and 30 are drawn without looking
questions.answer: All names go in a bin and 30 are drawn without looking
questions.solution: In a random sample every student has a fair chance of being chosen. Drawing names from a bin of all names does that. The other groups leave most students no chance.

solve.answer: All names go in a bin and 30 are drawn without looking
solve.work: Drawing names from a bin without looking gives every student an equal chance; the others are convenience or select groups.

questions.skill: Population and sample
questions.stem: A city has 50,000 voters. A poll of 400 randomly chosen voters finds that 56% favor a new bridge. Which of these is a sample statistic?
choices: The 56% of polled voters who favor the bridge
The percent of all voters who favor the bridge
questions.answer: The 56% of polled voters who favor the bridge
questions.solution: A statistic is a number computed from a sample. The 56% comes from the 400 polled voters. The percent of all voters is the unknown population value.

solve.answer: The 56% of polled voters who favor the bridge
solve.work: A statistic describes the sample: the 56% of the 400 polled.

questions.skill: Random and biased sampling
questions.stem: What makes a sample random?
choices: The members are picked because they are easy to reach
Each member has a fair chance of being picked
The members are picked because they chose to volunteer
The members are picked to match what we expect to find
questions.answer: Each member has a fair chance of being picked
questions.solution: A random sample is chosen by chance, so no part of the population is favored. Choosing people who are easy to reach, who volunteer, or who fit an expectation can all favor some people.

solve.answer: Each member has a fair chance of being picked
solve.work: Random selection means each member has a (equal) chance of being picked; the others are volunteer, convenience or biased selection.

questions.skill: Estimate a count in the population from a sample
questions.stem: A school has 800 students. In a random sample of 100 students, 40 said they prefer pizza for lunch. Estimate how many of the 800 students prefer pizza.
questions.solution: 40 out of 100 is 40%. Estimate 40% of 800: $0.4 \times 800 = 320$.

questions.skill: Estimate a count in the population from a sample
questions.stem: An inspector randomly picks 60 light bulbs from a shipment of 2,000 bulbs. Three of the 60 are defective. Estimate how many bulbs in the shipment are defective.

questions.skill: Estimate a mean or total from a sample
questions.stem: A random sample of 5 plants from a greenhouse has heights of 12, 15, 14, 16 and 13 centimeters. Use the sample to estimate the mean height of all the plants in the greenhouse, in centimeters.
questions.solution: The sample mean is $\frac{12+15+14+16+13}{5} = \frac{70}{5} = 14$, which is the estimate for all the plants.

questions.skill: Estimate a percent or fraction from a sample
questions.stem: In a random sample of 20 students, 5 walk to school. Use the sample to estimate the fraction of all the students at the school who walk to school.
questions.solution: $\frac{5}{20} = \frac{1}{4}$ of the sample walk, so estimate that $\frac{1}{4}$ of all students walk.

questions.skill: Estimate a percent or fraction from a sample
questions.stem: A random sample of 50 apples from a truckload contains 2 bruised apples. Estimate the percent of all the apples in the truckload that are bruised.
questions.solution: $\frac{2}{50} = 0.04$, which is 4%. Estimate that 4% of the apples in the truckload are bruised.

questions.skill: Population and sample
questions.stem: Why is a sample often used to learn about a population?
choices: Checking every member would take too much time or money
A sample always gives the exact value for the population
A sample is more accurate than checking everyone
A population is usually too small to measure
questions.answer: Checking every member would take too much time or money
questions.solution: Samples are used because checking a whole population is often slow or costly. A sample gives an estimate, not the exact value.

solve.answer: Checking every member would take too much time or money
solve.work: Sampling saves time and money compared with a census; the other options are false.

questions.skill: Random and biased sampling
questions.stem: A surveyor wants to know whether the residents of a town want a new skate park. She asks the first 40 people she meets at the town's existing skate park. Why might her results fail to represent the town?
choices: She asked too many people for such a small town
She asked about a topic that residents do not care about
She should have asked only the adults who live in town
Skate park visitors are not typical of all residents
questions.answer: Skate park visitors are not typical of all residents
questions.solution: People at a skate park are more likely to want another one than other residents are. Not every resident had a chance of being asked, so the sample is biased.

solve.answer: Skate park visitors are not typical of all residents
solve.work: People at a skate park are more likely to favor skate parks: convenience sample not representative.

questions.skill: Sampling variability and sample size
questions.stem: Two random samples are taken from the same large population to estimate its mean. One sample has 20 items and the other has 200 items. Which statement is most likely true?
choices: Both samples must give exactly the same mean as each other
The sample of 20 is more reliable because it is easier to check
The sample of 200 usually gives a closer estimate
The sample of 200 is biased because it is so large
questions.answer: The sample of 200 usually gives a closer estimate
questions.solution: Larger random samples vary less from sample to sample, so their means tend to be closer to the population mean. Size does not cause bias.

solve.answer: The sample of 200 usually gives a closer estimate
solve.work: Larger random samples have less variability, so the 200-item sample usually estimates closer.

questions.skill: Sampling variability and sample size
questions.stem: Maya and Leo each take a random sample of 50 beads from the same box of 1,000 beads. Maya finds 18 red beads and Leo finds 22 red beads. Which statement is best?
choices: One of the two must have made a counting mistake
Random samples from one box can give different counts
Leo's sample is better because it has more red beads
Both samples must always contain the same number of red beads
questions.answer: Random samples from one box can give different counts
questions.solution: Chance decides which beads land in each sample, so counts vary from sample to sample. Neither result is wrong.

solve.answer: Random samples from one box can give different counts
solve.work: Sampling variability: random samples from one box differ.

questions.skill: What a sample can and cannot tell us
questions.stem: A random sample of 100 students from a school of 1,500 finds that 62 of them prefer to take tests online. Which conclusion is best supported?
choices: About 62% of all students probably prefer online tests
Exactly 930 students at the school prefer online tests
Exactly 62 students at the school prefer online tests
Students at every other school also prefer online tests
questions.answer: About 62% of all students probably prefer online tests
questions.solution: The sample suggests about 62% of the school prefers online tests, though the true value may be a little different. It cannot give an exact count, and it says nothing about other schools.

solve.answer: About 62% of all students probably prefer online tests
solve.work: 62/100 = 62% is an estimate for the school, not exact, and not for other schools.

questions.skill: Random and biased sampling
questions.stem: Why do statisticians prefer a random sample to a sample of volunteers?
choices: Volunteers are usually too busy to answer the questions
A random sample is always larger than a volunteer sample
A random sample always matches the population exactly
Random selection favors no part of the population
questions.answer: Random selection favors no part of the population
questions.solution: Volunteers often share a strong opinion, which can skew results. A random sample gives every member a fair chance, so it tends to represent the population.

solve.answer: Random selection favors no part of the population
solve.work: Random selection avoids favoring any part of the population; volunteers self-select.

questions.skill: Estimate a count in the population from a sample
questions.stem: In a random sample of 600 residents of a town, 150 said they support building a new library. The town has 12,000 residents. Estimate how many residents support the library.
questions.solution: $\frac{150}{600} = \frac{1}{4}$ of the sample support it. Estimate $\frac{1}{4} \times 12000 = 3000$ residents.

questions.skill: Estimate a percent or fraction from a sample
questions.stem: A random sample of 90 commuters in a city finds that 27 of them ride a bike to work. Estimate the percent of all the commuters in the city who ride a bike to work.

questions.skill: Estimate a mean or total from a sample
questions.stem: A town has 5,000 households. A random sample of 8 households has 2, 0, 3, 1, 4, 2, 1 and 3 pets. Use the sample mean to estimate the total number of pets in all 5,000 households.
questions.solution: The sample total is 16 pets, so the mean is $\frac{16}{8} = 2$ pets per household. Estimate $2 \times 5000 = 10000$ pets.

questions.skill: Estimate a count in the population from a sample
questions.stem: A bag holds 500 marbles and is well mixed. A student draws a marble, records its color and puts it back, 40 times. Fourteen of the draws are red. Estimate how many of the 500 marbles are red.
questions.solution: $\frac{14}{40} = 0.35$ of the draws were red. Estimate $0.35 \times 500 = 175$ red marbles.

questions.skill: Random and biased sampling
questions.stem: A company wants to estimate the mean income of the households in a city. Which plan is most likely to give biased results?
choices: Choosing 500 households by random number from a list of all households
Choosing every 100th household from a complete list after a random start
Asking only the customers of an expensive jewelry store
Choosing 20 neighborhoods by chance, then households within each by chance
questions.answer: Asking only the customers of an expensive jewelry store
questions.solution: Customers of an expensive jewelry store are likely to have higher incomes than the city as a whole, so the sample is biased. The other plans give every household a fair chance.

solve.answer: Asking only the customers of an expensive jewelry store
solve.work: Customers of an expensive jewelry store over-represent high incomes; the others are random designs.

questions.skill: Sampling variability and sample size
questions.stem: A random sample of 400 voters finds that 52% favor Candidate A. A reporter writes, "Exactly 52% of all voters favor Candidate A." What is wrong with this statement?
choices: A sample of 400 voters can never be used to estimate anything
A sample gives an estimate, so the true percent may differ
The sample should have been chosen from voters who favor Candidate A
52% is too small a number to report from a poll
questions.answer: A sample gives an estimate, so the true percent may differ
questions.solution: A random sample gives a good estimate, but not the exact percent for all voters. Another random sample could give a different percent.

solve.answer: A sample gives an estimate, so the true percent may differ
solve.work: A sample statistic estimates the parameter; the true percent may differ.

questions.skill: What a sample can and cannot tell us
questions.stem: A random sample of 40 eleventh graders is chosen from one high school. To which group can the results most reasonably be applied?
choices: All eleventh graders at that high school
All eleventh graders in the country
All students at every high school in the district
questions.answer: All eleventh graders at that high school
questions.solution: Results from a random sample apply to the population it was drawn from: the eleventh graders at that school. Going beyond that group is not supported.

solve.answer: All eleventh graders at that high school
solve.work: The sample was drawn from that school only, so results generalize to its eleventh graders.

questions.skill: Random and biased sampling
questions.stem: To estimate how many hours a week the students at a school use their phones, Plan A chooses 100 students at random from the school roster. Plan B posts a link and uses the first 500 students who answer. Which plan should give a better estimate, and why?
choices: Plan B, because a larger sample always removes bias
Plan B, because students who volunteer answer more honestly
Plan A, because a smaller sample is easier to check
Plan A, because every student has a fair chance of being chosen
questions.answer: Plan A, because every student has a fair chance of being chosen
questions.solution: Plan B's volunteers may differ from the other students, and a larger sample does not fix that bias. Plan A is random, so its sample tends to represent the school.

solve.answer: Plan A, because every student has a fair chance of being chosen
solve.work: Plan A is a simple random sample; Plan B is voluntary response and biased regardless of size.

questions.skill: Random and biased sampling
questions.stem: A student council wants honest opinions about the cafeteria. Which survey question is most likely to bias the answers?
choices: How would you rate the cafeteria on a scale from 1 to 5?
Which meal served in the cafeteria do you like best?
Do you agree that the awful cafeteria must be fixed?
How many days a week do you eat lunch in the cafeteria?
questions.answer: Do you agree that the awful cafeteria must be fixed?
questions.solution: The wording "awful, crowded" pushes people toward agreeing. A fair question uses neutral words, even if the sample itself is random.

solve.answer: Do you agree that the awful cafeteria must be fixed?
solve.work: "awful" and "must be fixed" lead the respondent.

questions.skill: Estimate a count in the population from a sample
questions.stem: A random sample of 250 batteries from a shipment of 12,000 batteries has 7 dead batteries. Estimate how many batteries in the shipment are dead.
questions.solution: $\frac{7}{250} = 0.028$ of the sample are dead. Estimate $0.028 \times 12000 = 336$ dead batteries.

questions.skill: Sampling variability and sample size
questions.stem: Five random samples of 25 students each are taken from the same large school. Their mean test scores are 71, 68, 74, 70 and 67. Combine the five samples to give the best single estimate of the mean test score of the whole school.
questions.solution: All samples are the same size, so the combined mean is the average of the five means: $\frac{71+68+74+70+67}{5} = \frac{350}{5} = 70$.

solve.work: Equal sample sizes (25 each), so the pooled mean is the mean of the means: (71+68+74+70+67)/5 = 350/5 = 70.

questions.skill: Estimate a mean or total from a sample
questions.stem: A random sample of 40 students from a school of 1,500 students did an average of 6.4 hours of homework per week. Use the sample to estimate the total hours of homework per week done by all 1,500 students.
questions.solution: Estimate the mean for the whole school as 6.4 hours. Then the total is $6.4 \times 1500 = 9600$ hours.

solve.work: Estimate total = mean x population = 6.4 x 1500 = 9600.

questions.skill: Identify a sample survey, an experiment or an observational study
questions.stem: A researcher asks 200 randomly chosen adults how many hours they sleep each night and writes down their answers. What type of study is this?
questions.solution: The researcher asks questions of a sample of people to learn about a population. That is a sample survey.

solve.work: Researcher only asks a random sample questions and records answers; no treatment imposed. Sample survey.

questions.skill: Identify a sample survey, an experiment or an observational study
questions.stem: A scientist randomly puts 40 plants into two groups. One group gets a new fertilizer and the other gets none. She then measures how much each plant grows. What type of study is this?
questions.solution: The scientist decides which plants get the fertilizer and compares the results. A study in which the researcher applies a treatment is an experiment.

solve.work: Random assignment of plants to fertilizer vs none, then measure growth: experiment.

questions.skill: Identify a sample survey, an experiment or an observational study
questions.stem: A researcher looks at the health records of 300 adults and compares the blood pressure of those who already exercise often with those who do not. No one is asked to change what they do. What type of study is this?
questions.solution: The researcher only observes what people already do and does not assign any treatment. That is an observational study.

solve.work: Uses existing records, compares groups who already exercise; nothing imposed: observational study.

questions.skill: Purpose of each type of study
questions.stem: What is the main purpose of a sample survey?
choices: To show that a treatment causes changes in people
To assign people to treatment groups by a random draw
To estimate a fact about a population from a sample
To change the behavior of the people who are studied
questions.answer: To estimate a fact about a population from a sample
questions.solution: A sample survey asks some members of a population so that we can estimate a fact about the whole population.

solve.answer: To estimate a fact about a population from a sample
solve.work: A sample survey estimates a population characteristic from a sample.

questions.skill: Purpose of each type of study
questions.stem: Which type of study is designed to find out whether a treatment causes a change?
questions.solution: Only in an experiment does the researcher assign the treatment, which is what lets us test for cause and effect.

solve.work: Only an experiment (imposed treatment, ideally randomized) can establish cause.

questions.skill: What conclusions each type of study allows
questions.stem: A well-designed experiment uses random assignment. What can it show about the treatment?
choices: Whether the treatment causes a change
Only that two things are linked together
What a whole population thinks about it
That the sample is large enough
questions.answer: Whether the treatment causes a change
questions.solution: Random assignment makes the groups alike before the treatment, so a difference afterwards can be traced to the treatment. This allows a cause-and-effect conclusion.

solve.answer: Whether the treatment causes a change
solve.work: Random assignment lets an experiment show causation.

questions.skill: Randomization in sample surveys
questions.stem: A school has 500 students. Which of these is a random sample of 30 students?
choices: The first 30 students to walk in on Monday
Thirty students from the school chess club
Thirty students who are friends of the researcher
Thirty names drawn from a hat of all students
questions.answer: Thirty names drawn from a hat of all students
questions.solution: In a random sample, chance decides who is chosen and every student has an equal chance. Drawing names from a hat does this. The other plans let convenience or the researcher decide.

solve.answer: Thirty names drawn from a hat of all students
solve.work: Drawing names of all students from a hat gives every student a chance: random sample. Others are convenience/biased.

questions.skill: Randomization in sample surveys
questions.stem: A company emails a survey to 500 customers chosen at random from all 20,000 of its customers. What is the group of 500 customers called?
questions.solution: The 20,000 customers are the population. The 500 chosen to answer the survey are the sample.

solve.work: The 500 chosen from the 20,000 are the sample.

questions.skill: Randomization in experiments
questions.stem: In an experiment, what does random assignment mean?
choices: Each subject chooses their own treatment
Chance decides which treatment each subject receives
The researcher gives the treatment to those most likely to improve
The subjects are picked at random from the population
questions.answer: Chance decides which treatment each subject receives
questions.solution: Random assignment means chance, such as a coin flip or a random draw, decides who gets which treatment. Picking subjects at random from a population is random selection, which is different.

solve.answer: Chance decides which treatment each subject receives
solve.work: Random assignment: chance decides which treatment each subject gets (not random selection from population).

questions.skill: Identify a sample survey, an experiment or an observational study
questions.stem: Which of these is an experiment?
choices: Students are asked which of two study guides they prefer, then answers are compared
Scores of students who chose their own study guide are compared with the others
A teacher records which study guide each student already uses and their scores
Students are randomly given one of two study guides, then scores are compared
questions.answer: Students are randomly given one of two study guides, then scores are compared
questions.solution: In an experiment the researcher gives the treatment. Only in the first plan are students assigned a study guide by the researcher, and by chance. The others just ask or observe.

solve.answer: Students are randomly given one of two study guides, then scores are compared
solve.work: Only option A imposes the guide by random assignment; others are observational/survey.

questions.skill: Purpose of each type of study
questions.stem: A city wants to estimate the percentage of its residents who support building a new park. Which type of study fits best?
choices: An observational study of park visitors
questions.solution: The goal is to estimate a percentage for a whole population, so a sample survey of residents fits. No treatment is involved.

solve.work: Estimating a percentage of residents: sample survey.

questions.skill: Purpose of each type of study
questions.stem: A drug company wants to know whether a new drug lowers blood pressure more than an older drug. Which type of study fits best?
questions.solution: To see whether one drug causes a bigger drop, the researchers should assign the drugs to subjects at random and compare the results. That is an experiment.

solve.work: Comparing effect of two drugs: experiment (randomized).

questions.skill: Randomization in sample surveys
questions.stem: Why does a sample survey use random selection?
choices: So the sample can be split into treatment and control groups
So the people in the sample can pick how they answer
So every member has a chance to be chosen, avoiding bias
So the sample will agree with what the researcher expects
questions.answer: So every member has a chance to be chosen, avoiding bias
questions.solution: Random selection gives every member of the population a chance to be in the sample, which avoids bias and makes the sample likely to represent the population.

solve.answer: So every member has a chance to be chosen, avoiding bias
solve.work: Random selection gives every member a chance, avoiding bias.

questions.skill: Randomization in sample surveys
questions.stem: A radio station asks listeners to call in to vote on whether the city needs a new stadium. Why can its results not be trusted to describe all residents?
choices: The callers chose themselves, so it was not random
The station should have used an experiment instead
Too many people called in to vote on the stadium
The vote was about a stadium rather than a park
questions.answer: The callers chose themselves, so it was not random
questions.solution: People who choose to call in are not a random sample. They may feel more strongly than other residents, so the results can be biased.

solve.answer: The callers chose themselves, so it was not random
solve.work: Voluntary response sample: callers self-selected, not random.

questions.skill: What conclusions each type of study allows
questions.stem: An observational study finds that students who sleep more also earn higher grades. Which conclusion is justified?
choices: The study shows that more sleep causes students to get better grades
The study shows that better grades cause students to sleep longer
The study shows there is no link between sleep and grades
The study shows a link, but not that sleep causes better grades
questions.answer: The study shows a link, but not that sleep causes better grades
questions.solution: An observational study can show that two things are linked. Because no one was assigned to sleep more or less, it cannot show cause and effect.

solve.answer: The study shows a link, but not that sleep causes better grades

questions.skill: What conclusions each type of study allows
questions.stem: A random sample of 500 voters in a state is surveyed. To whom can the results be generalized?
choices: Only voters who chose to respond
questions.solution: Because the 500 voters were chosen at random from the state's voters, the results can reasonably be generalized to all voters in that state, but not beyond it.

solve.work: Random sample of the state's voters generalizes to all voters in the state.

questions.skill: Randomization in experiments
questions.stem: In an experiment, why is a control group included?
choices: To make sure every subject receives the treatment
To give a comparison group that gets no treatment
To make the experiment larger and more convincing
To let the subjects pick which group they join
questions.answer: To give a comparison group that gets no treatment
questions.solution: The control group shows what happens without the treatment, so the treatment group can be compared with it.

solve.answer: To give a comparison group that gets no treatment
solve.work: Control group gives a comparison that does not get the treatment.

questions.skill: Randomization in experiments
questions.stem: Before an experiment on a new study app, the researcher puts the students with the highest grades in the app group and everyone else in the other group. What is wrong with this plan?
choices: The app group should have had fewer students than the other group
The researcher should have used a survey of all the students instead
The groups were too large for the researcher to compare them
The groups already differed, so the app may not explain the result
questions.answer: The groups already differed, so the app may not explain the result
questions.solution: The app group already had higher grades, so a difference afterwards could be caused by that. Subjects should be assigned to groups at random so the groups are alike at the start.

solve.answer: The groups already differed, so the app may not explain the result
solve.work: Groups differed before treatment (highest grades in app group): confounding, so the app may not explain the result.

questions.skill: Identify a sample survey, an experiment or an observational study
questions.stem: A doctor flips a coin to decide whether each of 60 patients gets a new pill or a sugar pill, then compares recovery times. Which feature shows this is an experiment rather than an observational study?
choices: The doctor decided which treatment each patient received
The patients were measured after they took the treatment
The study compared two groups of patients with each other
The sample was made up of exactly 60 patients in all
questions.answer: The doctor decided which treatment each patient received
questions.solution: Measuring afterwards, having two groups and having 60 patients can all happen in an observational study. What makes it an experiment is that the researcher assigned the treatment, here by a coin flip.

solve.answer: The doctor decided which treatment each patient received
solve.work: The doctor (by coin) imposed which treatment each got: that makes it an experiment.

questions.skill: Identify a sample survey, an experiment or an observational study
questions.stem: A researcher randomly selects 100 students from a school. Each student then chooses whether to join a tutoring program, and she compares the grades of those who joined with those who did not. Which statement is correct?
choices: It is an experiment, because the students were chosen at random
It is an experiment, because two groups were compared
It is an observational study, because the researcher did not assign the treatment
It is a sample survey, because grades were collected
questions.answer: It is an observational study, because the researcher did not assign the treatment
questions.solution: Random selection of students does not make it an experiment. The students chose for themselves whether to join, so the researcher did not assign the treatment. It is an observational study.

solve.answer: It is an observational study, because the researcher did not assign the treatment
solve.work: Students chose themselves whether to join; researcher did not assign: observational study.

questions.skill: Purpose of each type of study
questions.stem: Researchers want to know whether smoking is linked to lung disease, but it would be unethical to make people smoke. Which type of study can they use?
choices: A study where the researcher assigns who smokes
questions.solution: Researchers cannot ethically assign people to smoke, so they observe people who already do and compare them with those who do not. That is an observational study.

solve.work: Cannot ethically assign smoking: observational study.

questions.skill: Purpose of each type of study
questions.stem: Which question is best answered by an experiment rather than an observational study?
choices: Does a new fertilizer make tomato plants produce more fruit?
What fraction of voters in a county prefer a candidate?
Do taller students tend to score higher on a reading test?
How many hours of television do teenagers watch in a week?
questions.answer: Does a new fertilizer make tomato plants produce more fruit?
questions.solution: Asking whether a fertilizer produces more fruit is a question about cause and effect, so the researcher applies the fertilizer to some plants and not others. The other questions describe or compare things as they already are.

solve.answer: Does a new fertilizer make tomato plants produce more fruit?
solve.work: Effect of fertilizer on fruit can be tested by assigning fertilizer: experiment.

questions.skill: What conclusions each type of study allows
questions.stem: A study finds that towns with more ice cream sales also have more drownings. Why can this study not show that ice cream sales cause drownings?
choices: The study did not include enough towns with ice cream sales
The towns in the study were chosen at random from a list
Drownings are too rare to be counted in a study like this
A third factor, like hot weather, may cause both of them
questions.answer: A third factor, like hot weather, may cause both of them
questions.solution: This is an observational study, so it can show a link but not a cause. Hot weather could lead to both more ice cream sales and more swimming, and so more drownings.

solve.answer: A third factor, like hot weather, may cause both of them

questions.skill: What conclusions each type of study allows
questions.stem: A survey of randomly selected adults finds that pet owners report being happier than other adults. Can the researcher conclude that owning a pet makes people happier?
choices: Yes, because the adults in the survey were chosen at random
No, because no one was assigned to own a pet, so it shows only a link
Yes, because the survey had a very large number of respondents
No, because the survey should have asked children and not adults
questions.answer: No, because no one was assigned to own a pet, so it shows only a link
questions.solution: Random selection lets us generalize to the population, but it does not show cause. Cause and effect needs an experiment in which owning a pet is randomly assigned.

solve.answer: No, because no one was assigned to own a pet, so it shows only a link
solve.work: No one assigned to own a pet; survey shows only association.

questions.skill: What conclusions each type of study allows
questions.stem: Eight teachers each choose which of two reading programs to use in their class, and test scores are compared. Why can a difference in scores not be credited to the programs?
choices: Eight teachers is too few to compare the two programs fairly
Teachers who choose may differ in ways that also affect scores
Both programs were used in the same school during the study
Test scores cannot be compared from one class to another
questions.answer: Teachers who choose may differ in ways that also affect scores
questions.solution: The teachers chose the programs themselves, so teacher skill or class makeup could explain a difference. Programs should be assigned at random.

solve.answer: Teachers who choose may differ in ways that also affect scores
solve.work: Self-selection by teachers: teachers who choose may differ in ways affecting scores (confounding).

questions.skill: Randomization in sample surveys
questions.stem: A school has 300 freshmen and 200 sophomores. A principal wants a random sample of 50 students that contains the same share of each grade as the school, choosing at random within each grade. How many freshmen should be in the sample?
questions.solution: Freshmen are $\frac{300}{500} = 60\%$ of the students, and $60\%$ of 50 is 30. So the sample should contain 30 freshmen, chosen at random from the freshmen.

questions.skill: Randomization in sample surveys
questions.stem: A factory makes 2,400 items in a day. An inspector picks a random starting item from the first 20 items and then checks every 20th item after that. How many items does the inspector check in the day?
questions.solution: The inspector checks one item in every 20, so $2400 \div 20 = 120$ items. The random starting point keeps the choice of items from following a pattern.

solve.work: Systematic sample: 2400/20 = 120 items checked (one in each block of 20).

questions.skill: Randomization in experiments
questions.stem: In an experiment, 36 subjects are placed into 18 matched pairs. A coin flip in each pair decides which person gets the treatment, and the other is the control. How many subjects get the treatment?
questions.solution: Each pair has exactly one treated person, so there are 18 treated subjects and 18 controls.

solve.work: One of each of 18 pairs gets treatment: 18.

questions.skill: Estimate a population value from a sample
questions.stem: A random sample of 80 students from a school of 1200 finds that 20 ride the bus. Estimate the proportion of all students at the school who ride the bus.
questions.solution: The sample proportion is $20 \div 80 = 0.25$. It is used to estimate the proportion for the whole school.

questions.skill: Margin of error for a proportion
questions.stem: The standard deviation of many simulated sample proportions is 0.03. The margin of error is 2 standard deviations. What is the margin of error?
questions.solution: Margin of error $= 2 \times 0.03 = 0.06$.

questions.skill: How sample size changes the margin of error
questions.stem: A pollster takes a larger random sample instead of a smaller one, with everything else the same. What happens to the margin of error?
questions.solution: Larger samples vary less from the population value, so the margin of error gets smaller. It never becomes zero.

solve.work: Margin of error shrinks as sample size grows (∝ 1/√n).

questions.skill: Estimate a population value from a sample
questions.stem: Which sample would best allow a margin of error to be used to estimate the opinion of all 2000 students in a school?
choices: A random sample of 100 students from the roster
The first 100 students to arrive at school one morning
The 100 students in the school chess club
The 100 students who answered a post on the school website
questions.answer: A random sample of 100 students from the roster
questions.solution: A margin of error describes random sampling variation, so it needs a random sample. The other groups are not random and can be biased.

solve.answer: A random sample of 100 students from the roster
solve.work: Only a random sample from the roster supports a margin of error; the others are convenience/voluntary samples.

questions.skill: Build or read an interval from an estimate and margin of error
questions.stem: A random sample gives a mean of 8.4 hours of sleep, with a margin of error of 0.6 hours. What is the upper end of the interval, in hours?
questions.solution: Add the margin of error to the sample mean: $8.4 + 0.6 = 9.0$ hours.

questions.skill: Build or read an interval from an estimate and margin of error
questions.stem: A sample estimate gives an interval of 0.46 to 0.58 for a population proportion. What is the margin of error?
questions.solution: The margin of error is half the width of the interval: $(0.58 - 0.46) \div 2 = 0.06$.

questions.skill: Read a simulation of random samples
questions.stem: A simulation takes many random samples of the same size from a population. What does the spread of the sample results show?
choices: The exact value of the population proportion
Which people in the population were chosen
Whether the sample was picked without any bias
How much results vary from sample to sample
questions.answer: How much results vary from sample to sample
questions.solution: Different random samples give different results. The spread of the simulated results shows how much a sample result can vary by chance.

solve.answer: How much results vary from sample to sample
solve.work: The spread of sample results shows sampling variability.

questions.skill: Read a simulation of random samples
questions.stem: A simulation takes 10 random samples from a population. The sample proportions are $0.36$, $0.42$, $0.44$, $0.38$, $0.40$, $0.46$, $0.34$, $0.40$, $0.42$ and $0.38$. Use their mean as the estimate of the population proportion. What is it?
questions.solution: The sum is $4.00$. The mean is $4.00 \div 10 = 0.40$.

questions.skill: Build or read an interval from an estimate and margin of error
questions.stem: A poll reports that 48% of voters favor a measure, with a margin of error of 4 percentage points. Which interval is most likely to contain the percent of all voters who favor it?
questions.solution: The interval is $48 \pm 4$, which is 44% to 52%.

questions.skill: Build or read an interval from an estimate and margin of error
questions.stem: A poll estimates that 62% of students walk to school, with a margin of error of 3 percentage points. What is the lower end of the interval, in percent?
questions.solution: The interval is the estimate plus or minus the margin of error: $62 - 3 = 59$ to $62 + 3 = 65$. The lower end is 59.

questions.skill: Build or read an interval from an estimate and margin of error
questions.stem: Simulated sample means for the weight of a bag of apples have a standard deviation of 0.75 pounds. A random sample has a mean of 52 pounds. Using a margin of error of 2 standard deviations, what is the lower end of the interval, in pounds?
questions.solution: Margin of error $= 2(0.75) = 1.5$. Lower end $= 52 - 1.5 = 50.5$ pounds.

questions.skill: Margin of error for a proportion
questions.stem: A random sample of 100 people has a sample proportion of 0.9. Use margin of error $= 2\sqrt{\frac{p(1 - p)}{n}}$, with $p$ the sample proportion, to find the margin of error in percentage points.
questions.solution: $\frac{0.9 \cdot 0.1}{100} = 0.0009$ and $\sqrt{0.0009} = 0.03$. The margin of error is $2(0.03) = 0.06$, or 6 percentage points.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion using the margin of error
questions.stem: A company claims that 35% of customers prefer its brand. A random sample of 200 customers finds that 42% prefer it, with a margin of error of 4 percentage points. What does this say about the claim?
choices: The claim is supported, since 42% is within 10 points of 35%
The claim is supported, since the sample percent is above 35%
The claim is proven false, since 35% is not equal to 42%
The claim is not supported, since 35% is outside 38% to 46%
